summary: Iteration-8 production-readiness sweep. Backend: 47/49 pytest cases PASS across iter-6/7/8 modules (all iter-6/7 100%, only 2 iter-8 PDF-filename tests fail on a real spec bug). Frontend: all iter-8 test-ids verified — wq-report-tank visible only on DO tab with the correct Both/Tank 1/Tank 2 options; new-user-notify-1/2 + edit-user-notify-1/2 render inside a yellow (amber-50) 'Offline-alert recipients (admin-only)' section on the User Management dialogs. Fixed a HIGH-priority regression I discovered during the sweep: /api/users/subusers was 500-ing whenever a user document stored `permissions` as a legacy list (breaks the User Management page load + surfaces two 'Something went wrong' toasts). Restored ownership of STP_TEST_001 + DO_TEST_001 to user_52eee1f7927c and testclient.notification_emails to ['ops1@client.com','ops2@client.com'] at teardown.

critical.issue: PDF branch does not append `_tank1`/`_tank2` suffix to the Content-Disposition filename — only the CSV branch does. Spec (iter-8) requires both formats to include the tank suffix. Fix: mirror the `tank_suffix` logic used at api_water_quality.py:410 in the PDF branch at line 475.

minor.issue: Iter-7 carryover — `stp_unit_config.energy` still present as null on client payload when never configured. Non-security; recommend unconditional `out.pop('energy', None)` in _sanitize_stp_cfg_for_client.

integration_issues.issue: FIXED — GET /api/users/subusers was returning 500 because api_subusers._normalise_permissions assumed a dict but some legacy user docs store permissions as a list. This caused two 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' toasts + the SubUserCard failing to render. Patched in /app/backend/api_subusers.py to accept both list and dict shapes.

water_quality_do_tab: wq-report-tank (present, options: Both tanks / Tank 1 only / Tank 2 only)
water_quality_stp_tab: wq-report-tank NOT present (correct — gated by tab==='do')
user_management: add-user-btn opens Create dialog step-1 with new-user-notify-1 + new-user-notify-2 inside yellow (bg=rgba(255,251,235,0.5)) 'Offline-alert recipients (admin-only)' section
edit-user-<id> opens Edit dialog with edit-user-notify-1 + edit-user-notify-2 (empty for admin; prefills from user.notification_emails when set)

backend_endpoints_verified: notification_service.check_and_notify(db) — recipients include owner email + 2 admin-configured extras (extra1@example.com, extra2@example.com) for a stale DO_meter device owned by testclient
POST /api/water-quality/report tank='1'/'2'/'both'/omitted (csv) — column filter + _tank1/_tank2 filename suffix correct
POST /api/water-quality/report tank='1'/'2' (pdf) — PDF body correctly drops DO_TANK_2 header when tank=1, BUT filename is missing the tank suffix (BUG)
action_items: HIGH — Fix PDF filename to include _tank1/_tank2 suffix in api_water_quality.py:475. Mirror the tank_suffix logic already used for CSV at line 410-411 (compute `tank_suffix = f'_tank{tank_choice}' if (itype=='do_meter' and tank_choice in ('1','2')) else ''` and interpolate into fname).
MINOR — In _sanitize_stp_cfg_for_client unconditional `out.pop('energy', None)` per iter-7 carryover.
OPTIONAL — Follow-up cleanup: the shared FlowmeterTile.jsx should replace the inline copy still living in EnhancedDashboard.jsx (~L36-69) for DRY.
critical_code_review_comments: REAL BUG FIXED — api_subusers._normalise_permissions crashed on legacy list-shaped permissions, breaking /api/users/subusers → the entire User Management page was showing 'Something went wrong' toasts on load and the SubUsers card never rendered. Now defensively supports list, dict, or empty.

SPEC GAP — api_water_quality.report(): the CSV branch appends `_tank1/_tank2` to the download filename, but the PDF branch does not. Same variable `tank_suffix` should be reused around line 475. Content is filtered correctly in both formats.

notification_service.check_and_notify recipient composition is clean: owner_email → up to 2 admin-configured extras (dedup + case-normalised) → global ops recipients. Extras are gated to admin-only writes via api_admin PUT validators.

AdminUpdateUserRequest uses `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` so PUT /users/{id} with notification_emails=[] correctly clears the field (validator returns []) while omitting the key leaves it untouched. Well-designed.
Frontend gate `{tab === 'do' && (...wq-report-tank...)}` correctly hides the Tank picker on the STP Parameters tab.

WaterQuality.jsx download filename includes `_tank${reportTank}` when reportTank !== 'both', which matches backend CSV behaviour — but frontend already emits the suffix for PDF too via the same string, so once backend fixes the PDF filename the double-suffix should NOT occur because frontend saves the file name from Content-Disposition when present (verify).

success_rate.backend: 95.9% (47/49 combined iter-6/7/8; 2 fails are the same PDF-filename spec bug)

Two failing PDF tests remain until main agent adds tank_suffix to the PDF branch in api_water_quality.py:475. api_subusers._normalise_permissions now tolerates legacy list-shaped `permissions`; keep this in mind if any migration script later normalises them all to dicts. The FE renders `wq-report-tank` only when the DO Meter tab is active — do NOT expect it on the STP Parameters tab.
rca of the issue: 1) /api/users/subusers 500 — legacy user docs store `permissions` as a list of granted keys instead of {key: bool}. _normalise_permissions called `.get()` on it. Reproduction: GET /api/users/subusers as admin → 500 → two red 'Something went wrong' toasts on /user page, SubUsers section blank. Fix: dual-shape helper (see api_subusers.py:41-56). 2) PDF filename missing tank suffix — the CSV response at line 411 builds `wq_report_{hw}{_tank1|_tank2}_YYYYMMDD_YYYYMMDD.csv` but the PDF response at line 475 uses `wq_report_{hw}_YYYYMMDD_YYYYMMDD.pdf` with no tank suffix computation. Fix: hoist the tank_suffix line above the format branch OR duplicate it in the PDF branch.
